newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan surplus unlikely to rise much in future-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan surplus unlikely to rise much in future-MOF.

text.p: Japan's trade surplus is unlikely to increase significantly in the future, Japan's Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told reporters on Thursday.
"The trade surplus has fallen greatly and it is unlikely to rise in the future to the levels at which it used to be a problem," Ogawa told a regular news conference.

The Finance Ministry earlier on Thursday released Japan's trade data for March which showed that while the overall surplus fell, the politically sensitive surplus with the United States rose 11 percent year on year.
Ogawa added that it was important to look at the trend of the trade account, pointing out that Japan's trade surplus with the rest of the world peaked around 1992.

Asked how Tokyo would respond if the United States voiced its concern that Japan was trying to boost economic growth through exports, Ogawa said Japan will state that it is seeking economic growth centred around domestic demand.
U.S. President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto are due to meet later this month.
Asked if he was concerned about a slight drop in the growth in money supply in March, Ogawa said economic indicators fluctuate every month, adding, "it poses no problem".
Japan's money supply grew a preliminary 2.7 percent in March from a year earlier, compared with growth of 3.0 percent in February.
